research_question: In adults with overweight or obesity, what is the effect of a smartphone app intervention compared with no intervention or a minimal, non-app intervention on body weight in kilograms at short-term follow-up (3 to <6 months)?
control_label: No intervention or minimal non-app control
outcome_description: Body weight in kilograms at short-term follow-up (3 to <6 months, preferably 3-4 months, preferring change-from-baseline values over follow-up values)
positive_direction: Greater weight loss / reduction in body weight in the smartphone app intervention group compared to the control group
search_queries: smartphone app weight loss trial adults overweight obesity
mobile application body weight randomized controlled trial
smartphone intervention weight reduction comparison trial
inclusion_criteria: Adults (≥18 years) with overweight or obesity participating in an intervention involving a smartphone application targeting weight loss or weight management.
Empirical comparative trials comparing a smartphone app against a genuine no-intervention or minimal non-app control condition (such as usual care, waitlist, printed materials, or paper diaries).
Reporting quantitative body weight outcomes in kilograms at short-term follow-up (3 to <6 months).
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, study protocols, qualitative studies, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers are excluded).
No genuine non-app control comparison (e.g., studies where both arms receive a smartphone app or different versions of an app).
No quantitative body weight data in kilograms reported at short-term follow-up (3 to <6 months), or lacking convertible data (means, SDs, SEs, or 95% CIs).
Studies in pediatric/adolescent populations, non-overweight populations, or interventions completely unrelated to weight management.
moderators_to_extract: Control condition type (no intervention/waitlist vs minimal intervention/printed materials/usual care)
App delivery mode (standalone self-guided app vs app with human coaching/counseling)
Exact follow-up timepoint in weeks/months within the 3 to <6 month short-term window
Outcome data type (change from baseline vs post-intervention endpoint weight)
Baseline sample mean BMI or weight category
effect_size_note: Extract one endpoint per study at short-term follow-up (3 to <6 months, preferring 3-4 months). When a study reports both post-intervention weight and change-from-baseline weight, prioritize change-from-baseline data. Exclude non-weight outcomes and outcomes at 6 months or longer.
